nodes.description: Continued lipid accumulation, foam-cell death, and matrix remodeling produce a mature coronary atheroma with a necrotic lipid core beneath a fibrous cap. Expansion of the core and local plaque microenvironment can destabilize the cap and create a rupture-prone coronary lesion.

evidence.reference_title: The microenvironment of the atheroma expresses phenotypes of plaque instability.
evidence.snippet: the local arterial microenvironment of a stable atheroma promotes destabilizing conditions that result in the transition to an unstable atheroma.

evidence.reference_title: Single-Cell Gene-Regulatory Networks of Advanced Symptomatic Atherosclerosis.
evidence.snippet: Advanced stages of atherosclerosis progression and symptomatic carotid plaques were largely characterized by 3 smooth muscle cells (SMCs), and 3 macrophage subtype clusters with extracellular matrix organization/osteogenic (SMC), and M1-type proinflammatory/Trem2-high lipid-associated (macrophage) phenotypes.

evidence.reference_title: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis of mouse carotid artery under disturbed flow and human carotid plaques identifies key cell populations in atherosclerosis development.
evidence.snippet: Notable increases in VEGFA+ macrophages were discovered in the disturbed flow stimulation group, displaying a pronounced M1 pro-inflammatory phenotype associated with the severity of atherosclerosis and plaque stability.

evidence.reference_title: Single-Cell Gene-Regulatory Networks of Advanced Symptomatic Atherosclerosis.
evidence.snippet: By identifying and integrating the most gene-rich single-cell subclusters of atherosclerosis to date with a coronary artery disease framework of GRNs, GRN39 was identified and independently validated as being critical for the transformation of contractile SMCs into an osteogenic phenotype promoting advanced, symptomatic atherosclerosis.

nodes.description: In the inflamed coronary intima, vascular smooth muscle cells switch to a synthetic, migratory phenotype, proliferate, and organize extracellular matrix to build the fibrofatty plaque and its fibrous cap. This is the atomic smooth-muscle-cell and matrix assembly step of coronary atheroma formation.

evidence.reference_title: From Cells to Plaques: The Molecular Pathways of Coronary Artery Calcification and Disease.
evidence.snippet: We examine the cellular and molecular processes that drive the formation of calcified plaques, highlighting the roles of inflammation, lipid accumulation, and smooth muscle cell proliferation.

evidence.reference_title: The microenvironment of the atheroma expresses phenotypes of plaque instability.
evidence.snippet: vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching through transdifferentiation and stem/progenitor cell activation resulting in the promotion of inflammation, calcification, and secretion of extracellular matrix, altering fibrous cap structure, and necrotic core growth.

nodes.description: In the coronary arterial intima, endothelial injury and dysfunction permit infiltration and retention of apoB-containing lipoproteins in the subendothelial space. Retained and modified lipoproteins initiate local inflammation and monocyte recruitment, providing the coronary trigger for atheroma formation.
nodes.id: Coronary Endothelial Injury and Subendothelial LDL Retention

evidence.reference_title: The Role of Lipids and Lipoproteins in Atherosclerosis.
evidence.snippet: infiltration and retention of apoB containing lipoproteins in the artery wall is a critical initiating event that sparks an inflammatory response and promotes the development of atherosclerosis.

nodes.description: At atherosclerosis-prone arterial sites, disturbed flow is associated with endothelial stress and senescence, while reduced endothelial nitric-oxide biosynthesis represents the vasomotor dysfunction that impairs dilation. This nonconforming coronary endothelial-function branch is modeled separately from the conserved subendothelial apoB-retention trigger. The cited disturbed-flow evidence derives from mouse carotid arteries and human carotid plaques, so its transfer to coronary endothelial dysfunction is explicitly partial.

evidence.reference_title: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis of mouse carotid artery under disturbed flow and human carotid plaques identifies key cell populations in atherosclerosis development.
evidence.snippet: CD36 + positive ECs exhibited significant senescence phenotypes following disturbed flow stimulation.

evidence.reference_title: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis of mouse carotid artery under disturbed flow and human carotid plaques identifies key cell populations in atherosclerosis development.
evidence.snippet: Atherosclerosis tends to occur in regions of disturbed blood flow. This study explored how disturbed flow aggravates atherosclerosis using single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) datasets from mouse carotid arteries under disturbed flow and human carotid artery plaques.

nodes.description: In the coronary intima, recruited monocytes become macrophages and internalize retained apoB-containing lipoproteins, forming lipid-laden foam cells. Their inflammatory feed-forward loop promotes further lipoprotein oxidation, endothelial activation, monocyte recruitment, and foam-cell formation.
nodes.id: Monocyte Recruitment and Macrophage Foam Cell Formation

evidence.reference_title: The Role of Lipids and Lipoproteins in Atherosclerosis.
evidence.snippet: Internalization of the apoB containing lipoproteins by macrophages promotes foam cell formation, which is the hallmark of the fatty streak phase of atherosclerosis.

evidence.reference_title: The Role of Lipids and Lipoproteins in Atherosclerosis.
evidence.snippet: Macrophage inflammation results in enhanced oxidative stress and cytokine/chemokine secretion, causing more LDL/remnant oxidation, endothelial cell activation, monocyte recruitment, and foam cell formation.

nodes.description: Rupture of an unstable coronary atheroma, or endothelial erosion over it, exposes thrombogenic material and triggers platelet activation, coagulation, and thrombotic coronary occlusion, causing acute coronary syndrome and myocardial infarction.

evidence.reference_title: The microenvironment of the atheroma expresses phenotypes of plaque instability.
evidence.snippet: Destabilization is characterized by several different plaque phenotypes that cause major clinical events such as acute coronary syndrome and cerebrovascular strokes.

evidence.reference_title: The microenvironment of the atheroma expresses phenotypes of plaque instability.
